Subject: Clarify minimum spend / surge terms for Hosted API

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood's latency profile. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple of commercial items before we proceed:

- We need clarity on the minimum monthly/annual spend floor required for the usage-based hosted API. Is there a way to set a monthly minimum that rolls into an annual commitment?
- How do you handle overage when traffic spikes? Specifically: is there a separate "burst" rate, a multiplier over list on-demand pricing, or a true-up at the end of the month/quarter?
- Any limits on burst windows (e.g., 24/72 hours) or caps on the amount of burstable tokens?

Procurement also wants to understand if unused committed spend can bank or roll into the next period. If you can share a short term sheet or example math, that'd help us present to finance.

Thanks — Mia

Subject: Re: Clarify minimum spend / surge terms for Hosted API

Hi Mia — great question and glad the demo was useful. Putting a short, practical layout below so your procurement/finance team has concrete numbers to evaluate. Attaching a simple pricing matrix for illustration (pricing_matrix.csv).

High-level proposal (draft):
- Minimum spend (monthly): $30,000 USD (can be expressed as an annual prepay or 12x monthly commits).
- Commit tiers: modular; example shown in attachment (30k / 75k / 200k monthly token-equivalent tiers with stepped discounts).
- Burst / surge handling: on-demand overage billed at 1.6x list per-token rate for incremental tokens above committed usage, applicable up to 25% of committed tokens per month. Bursts beyond 25% trigger an elevated multiplier (2.5x) or an auto-escalation to Dedicated routing if requested.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up (calculate delta vs committed spend; apply credit or invoice).
- Banking / rollover: unconsumed committed spend can roll forward up to 1 month as credits; excess unused beyond that is forfeited unless annual prepay agreed.
- Short emergency buffer: one 7-day unlimited burst window per quarter available with prior notice (subject to capacity; suitable for coordinated launches).

Open negotiation points: exact multipliers, % burst allowance, and the length of credit rollover. If your procurement prefers annual minimums instead of monthly, we can convert to an annual committed amount with a moderate additional discount.

Next step: if this aligns roughly with what you need, I'll draft a termsheet for your legal & procurement to review.

Thanks,

Sergio / Karthik — thanks for the quick draft. A few notes from our side after an internal procurement sync:

1) The proposed 1.6x overage multiplier is a hard ask for us to reduce. Can Redwood consider 1.45x for the first 30% of burst above commit and a step to 2.0x thereafter? Our expected pattern is short spikes rather than sustained overages.
2) Procurement prefers an annual minimum (so we can budget centrally). They want assurance that unused committed dollars can be carried forward and applied against the next quarter or toward professional services (SOW).
3) Can we get a defined "burst window" guarantee (e.g., up to 72 hours per month as a recoverable buffer) rather than the one-off quarter window? That helps us plan launches.

I can share a draft PO once we have the term sheet updated.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Cole, Head of Infrastructure
Novaline

Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: suggested revisions for Novaline term sheet

Sergio / Laura — quick internal note to propose mechanics that are easier to justify to finance while keeping unit economics intact:

- Tiered overage bands: 0–20% over commit -> 1.45x list; 20–50% over commit -> 2.0x; >50% -> 3.0x (or require Dedicated evaluation).
- Offer monthly 72-hour burst window (per calendar month) for planned launches; unplanned bursts billed at overage bands.
- Rollover: allow up to 2 months of unused committed spend to carry forward for annual prepay customers.
- Annual prepay incentive: additional 6% discount on effective per-token rates and waive administrative fee for payment processing.

These preserve upside while addressing their asks about predictability. If we agree, I can incorporate these into a clean termsheet.

Karthik
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood - consolidated termsheet for Novaline (draft)

Hi Mia / Evan — attaching the consolidated termsheet with the adjustments we discussed (Redwood_Termsheet_Novaline_2026-07-09.pdf). Key commercial points summarized below for quick review: 

1) Minimum commitment: $360,000 USD annual (billed monthly as $30,000/mo or payable as annual prepay).
2) On-demand overage pricing: tiered approach — up to 30% over commit billed at 1.45x list; 30–60% at 2.0x; >60% triggers manual review / Dedicated.
3) Burst allowance: 72-hour window per calendar month for planned launches (no overage charge within the window for reasonable spike patterns).
4) Rollover: up to 2 months of unconsumed committed spend can be banked and applied to future invoices (annual prepay extends banking rules).
5) True-up cadence: quarterly true-up with netting.

Open items for your feedback: whether the 72-hour monthly window is sufficient, whether the 2-month rollover is acceptable, and whether procurement wants billing as monthly invoices or an annual prepay.

If the terms look good, please confirm and Evan can issue a PO; I'll route the clean SOW and DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks,
Sergio
